newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-SRI LANKA COLLAPSE AGAINST PAKISTAN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SRI LANKA COLLAPSE AGAINST PAKISTAN.

text.p: Sri Lanka lost three quick wickets for 17 runs in as many balls as they were bowled out for 239 by Pakistan in the opening match of the sixth Asia Cup on Monday.
The World Cup champions, sent in to bat by Pakistani captain Rameez Raja after he won the toss, cruised along merrily to reach 160 for 2 before the batting collapse began.
Sri Lanka lost their remaining eight wickets for only 79 runs off 94 balls.
Only opener Mavan Atapattu played a positive innings, scoring his fifth one-day half century before being run out for 80.

Atapattu's hit the score off 114 balls, including three hits to the boundary. He shared a 65-run second wicket partnership with Aravinda de Silva (34) before he was the seventh batsman to depart at 209 in the 45th over.
Pakistan were jubilant when they were able to get the key wicket of Sanath Jayasuriya's cheaply. The Sri Lankan opener, who hit one six, was restricted to 33 off 41 balls.
Jayasuriya also hit three fours before lofting Kabir Khan to mid-on where Rameez Raja took a superb catch running to his left.
Saqlain Mushtaq bowled an excellent line for Pakistan, claiming one wicket for 38 runs in his 10 overs.
